compounds.name: Noopept
compounds.description: A synthetic dipeptide-like compound with a small comparative clinical literature.
compounds.mechanism: Neurotrophin expression changes were reported in rat hippocampus; this does not demonstrate neurogenesis or disease prevention in people.
compounds.findings: A small comparative study evaluated cognitive impairment of vascular or traumatic origin against piracetam.
compounds.limits: The design and population do not establish enhancement in healthy adults.
compounds.kinetics: Human exposure and formulation-equivalence information remains limited in these sources.
compounds.risks: Reliable adverse-effect frequencies and long-term safety estimates are not established by this evidence set.
compounds.interactions: Human interaction studies are insufficient; mechanistic speculation cannot replace interaction data.

adverse.context: The small comparative clinical record cannot reliably identify uncommon or delayed harm.
Rat gene-expression findings are not a human safety assessment.

compounds.name: Phenibut
compounds.description: A GABA-related drug encountered in anxiety and sleep products, with a substantial toxicity record.
compounds.mechanism: GABA-B agonism contributes to central nervous system depression.
compounds.findings: Poison-center surveillance and clinical reports document acute toxicity and withdrawal; these are safety data, not evidence of cognitive benefit.
compounds.limits: Exposure reports are selected and sometimes involve other substances; their percentages are not risks per user.
compounds.kinetics: Clinical toxicity can outlast perceived effects; marketed-product identity and exposure are uncertain.
compounds.risks: Dependence, withdrawal, impaired consciousness, and respiratory depression are documented concerns.
compounds.interactions: Other CNS depressants may increase impairment and respiratory risk; direct combination-risk estimates are limited.

adverse.context: Observed in reported poison-center exposures, including single-substance cases.
A regional series included respiratory failure requiring airway support.
Anxiety, agitation and psychosis have been described after repeated use.

compounds.name: Tianeptine
compounds.description: An antidepressant in some jurisdictions that also has opioid pharmacology.
compounds.mechanism: Mu-opioid receptor agonism is experimentally established; older descriptions focused too narrowly on serotonin.
compounds.findings: A controlled trial found antidepressant effects in older patients with recurrent depression.
compounds.limits: Therapeutic clinical data cannot validate unregulated products or nonmedical cognitive-enhancement claims.
compounds.kinetics: Products, exposure patterns and coingredients differ between medical trials and reported poisonings.
compounds.risks: FDA reports serious toxicity, dependence and withdrawal associated with marketed tianeptine products.
compounds.interactions: Opioids, alcohol and other CNS depressants create additional concern; unverified coingredients complicate attribution.

adverse.effect: Respiratory depression and loss of consciousness
adverse.context: Severe toxicity is described in FDA safety information; product identity and coexposures can vary.
Documented with tianeptine misuse; not excluded by short therapeutic trials.

unknowns: Risk for any particular unregulated formulation
Safety of use for cognitive enhancement

compounds.name: Bromantane
compounds.description: An adamantane derivative studied for asthenia and neurasthenia.
compounds.mechanism: A precise human target-to-benefit mechanism is not established by the cited clinical studies.
compounds.findings: A Russian placebo comparison reported reduced asthenic symptoms; another study investigated EEG-related differences in response.
compounds.limits: Limited independent replication and reporting detail restrict generalization.
compounds.kinetics: The cited records do not establish a broadly validated human exposure model.
compounds.risks: A short study's lack of observed withdrawal cannot establish absence of addiction or long-term adverse effects.
compounds.interactions: Reliable clinical interaction studies are insufficient.

adverse.context: Short clinical observations do not resolve delayed or uncommon harm.
No withdrawal observed in one short study is narrower than proof of no addictive potential.

compounds.name: Semax
compounds.description: A synthetic peptide investigated in neurological disease and preclinical neurotrophin research.
compounds.mechanism: Changes in neurotrophin-related transcription were studied in rat ischemia models.
compounds.findings: A clinical stroke-rehabilitation study examined BDNF and functional measures.
compounds.limits: Selected patient studies do not demonstrate general cognitive enhancement; modified Semax derivatives are different compounds.
compounds.kinetics: Clinical formulation and route cannot be assumed equivalent to online preparations.
compounds.risks: Reliable frequencies for serious, delayed or formulation-specific adverse effects remain unresolved.
compounds.interactions: Human drug–peptide interaction data are inadequate.

adverse.context: The limited clinical record is inadequate to characterize uncommon or long-term reactions.
Data for Semax cannot establish safety of acetylated or amidated variants.

compounds.name: Selank
compounds.description: A synthetic peptide investigated for anxiety and neurasthenia.
compounds.mechanism: An exploratory study measured blood enkephalin-related biomarkers; a biomarker association is not a validated clinical target.
compounds.findings: A 62-patient comparison with medazepam reported anxiolytic findings.
compounds.limits: An active-comparator study of this size does not resolve efficacy against placebo or prove cognitive enhancement.
compounds.kinetics: Preparation, route and peptide modifications can change exposure; equivalence is unproven.
compounds.risks: The cited trial cannot establish frequencies of uncommon, immune-mediated or delayed harms.
compounds.interactions: Reliable clinical interaction studies are lacking.

adverse.context: Small comparative patient research cannot establish a comprehensive side-effect profile.
Original-compound findings do not establish safety of modified commercial derivatives.

compounds.name: Dihexa
compounds.description: An experimental compound with a major integrity warning in its foundational literature.
compounds.mechanism: The commonly cited HGF/c-Met mechanism paper was retracted in 2025; its findings should not be treated as established.
compounds.findings: The retraction notice documents withdrawal of the foundational 2014 mechanism study.
compounds.limits: Mechanism and benefit claims require independent validation. Findings from related compounds are not interchangeable.
compounds.kinetics: Reliable human pharmacokinetics are not established in the evidence curated here.
compounds.risks: No dependable human adverse-effect incidence or long-term safety estimate is available.

adverse.context: No reliable human safety assessment is provided by the cited evidence.
Retracted findings cannot establish clinical safety or predict an adverse-effect profile.

unknowns: Human safety, exposure and clinical benefit

integrity.note: The foundational 2014 HGF/c-Met mechanism paper was retracted in 2025. Its mechanistic conclusions are not treated as established evidence here. Independent studies, if any, require separate appraisal.

compounds.name: NSI-189
compounds.description: An investigational compound tested in major depressive disorder.
compounds.mechanism: Described as neurogenic in preclinical work; human benefit does not itself verify hippocampal neurogenesis.
compounds.findings: A 220-participant phase 2 trial did not meet its primary depression endpoint, despite exploratory secondary findings.
compounds.limits: Secondary outcomes and an earlier small study do not override the negative primary result.
compounds.kinetics: An early study characterized oral exposure in depressed patients.
compounds.risks: Short trials constrain long-term safety conclusions.
compounds.interactions: Dedicated interaction evidence is insufficient for broad real-world use.

adverse.context: Reported in the small phase 1b study in active and placebo groups; not automatically caused by treatment.
Reported during early clinical testing; small groups cannot establish a stable incidence.

compounds.name: Sunifiram
compounds.description: An experimental cognition-related compound studied in animal and laboratory models.
compounds.mechanism: Experimental results implicate AMPA-mediated neurotransmission; this is not proof of a selective direct receptor target in humans.
compounds.findings: Mouse amnesia experiments and rat hippocampal assays reported effects on learning-related signaling.
compounds.limits: Reversing experimentally induced amnesia does not demonstrate enhancement in healthy people.
compounds.kinetics: No reliable human pharmacokinetic model is established by the cited study.
compounds.risks: Human neurological, cardiovascular and reproductive safety remain unknown.
compounds.interactions: Human interaction studies are lacking; interactions cannot be inferred from the absence of case reports.

adverse.context: Animal behavioral findings do not establish a human safety profile.
Seizure or excitotoxicity risk is a mechanistic question, not a demonstrated incidence for this compound.

compounds.name: Unifiram
compounds.description: An experimental cognition-related compound studied in animal and laboratory models.
compounds.mechanism: Experimental results implicate AMPA-mediated neurotransmission; this is not proof of a selective direct receptor target in humans.
compounds.findings: Mouse amnesia experiments and rat hippocampal assays reported effects on learning-related signaling.
compounds.limits: Reversing experimentally induced amnesia does not demonstrate enhancement in healthy people.
compounds.kinetics: No reliable human pharmacokinetic model is established by the cited study.
compounds.risks: Human neurological, cardiovascular and reproductive safety remain unknown.
compounds.interactions: Human interaction studies are lacking; interactions cannot be inferred from the absence of case reports.

adverse.context: Animal behavioral findings do not establish a human safety profile.
Seizure or excitotoxicity risk is a mechanistic question, not a demonstrated incidence for this compound.

compounds.name: Phenylpiracetam
compounds.description: A phenyl-substituted racetam investigated in neurological patient populations.
compounds.mechanism: Clinical symptom changes do not validate a specific receptor mechanism.
compounds.findings: An observational program reported improved asthenic symptoms in patients with chronic brain ischemia.
compounds.limits: Without randomized control, natural history, expectancy and cointerventions can influence outcomes.
compounds.kinetics: Clinical exposure and stereoisomer-specific pharmacology require further characterization.
compounds.risks: Reliable adverse-effect rates and long-term risks are not defined by the cited observational record.

adverse.context: An observational improvement report cannot establish comprehensive safety.
The cited clinical program does not establish long-duration safety in healthy people.

compounds.name: Aniracetam
compounds.description: A racetam with historical dementia trials and small human pharmacokinetic studies.
compounds.mechanism: Glutamatergic effects are proposed; the clinical mechanism is not settled by the cited trials.
compounds.findings: A 109-patient placebo-controlled dementia study reported benefits on psychobehavioral measures.
compounds.limits: Historical dementia findings do not establish healthy-person enhancement or current standard-of-care effectiveness.
compounds.kinetics: A small volunteer study evaluated oral formulations and exposure.
compounds.risks: Favorable short-study tolerability cannot exclude rare or delayed adverse effects.
compounds.interactions: Reliable contemporary interaction characterization is limited in these sources.

adverse.context: Historical tolerability statements do not give a complete modern risk estimate.
A studied formulation's exposure cannot be assumed for unverified products.

compounds.name: Fasoracetam
compounds.description: An investigational compound examined in genetically selected adolescents with ADHD.
compounds.mechanism: The clinical program targeted altered mGluR-network signaling; general nootropic claims are broader than the study.
compounds.findings: A 30-person early study reported symptom improvement after a single-blind placebo week.
compounds.limits: Small size, sequential design and genetic selection limit causal inference and generalization.
compounds.kinetics: The trial characterized oral exposure in its selected population.
compounds.risks: Adverse events occurred during testing, without a clear active-week excess over placebo week.

adverse.context: Reported across study weeks; frequencies did not differ between placebo and active weeks.

adverse.effect: Dizziness with brief loss of consciousness
adverse.context: Occurred during the study; investigators did not attribute serious events to the drug. Causality remains uncertain.

compounds.name: Alpha-GPC
compounds.description: A choline-containing compound with small cognition trials and an observational vascular safety signal.
compounds.mechanism: It supplies a choline precursor; this does not imply universally beneficial cholinergic effects.
compounds.findings: A small acute crossover trial assessed cognition. A large Korean prescription cohort found an association with subsequent stroke.
compounds.limits: The cohort cannot prove causation. A September 2026 correction fixed diagnostic-code descriptions and author information.
compounds.kinetics: Acute supplement exposure differs from years of prescription exposure.
compounds.risks: The stroke association warrants investigation but is not a randomized estimate of causal risk.
compounds.interactions: Combination effects with cholinergic medicines remain incompletely quantified.

adverse.context: Observed in older prescription users; confounding by indication and residual confounding remain possible.

adverse.effect: Long-term risk in young supplement users unknown
adverse.context: Neither the small acute trial nor older-patient cohort directly quantifies that setting.

unknowns: Whether the stroke association is causal

compounds.name: Huperzine A
compounds.description: A cholinesterase inhibitor investigated in Alzheimer disease.
compounds.findings: A 210-person phase 2 trial did not meet its primary cognitive endpoint; secondary findings were insufficient to establish benefit.
compounds.limits: Disease-specific trial findings do not establish enhancement in healthy people.
compounds.kinetics: Clinical exposure is formulation-dependent; botanical mixtures are not equivalent to the isolated study compound.
compounds.risks: Nausea was an important tolerability problem in the cited trial.
compounds.interactions: Other cholinesterase inhibitors may add cholinergic effects; this is a pharmacologic concern, not a quantified combination trial result.

adverse.context: Nausea was the most common reason for intolerance in the phase 2 trial.
Class-related effects require assessment; the trial was too small to exclude uncommon harms.

compounds.name: Methylphenidate
compounds.description: A prescription stimulant used in ADHD and selected sleep disorders.
compounds.findings: Clinical evidence and labeling concern diagnosed conditions; healthy-person cognitive enhancement is a separate question.
compounds.limits: Different release formulations have different exposure profiles.
compounds.kinetics: Immediate- and extended-release products are not pharmacokinetically interchangeable.
compounds.risks: Cardiovascular, sleep, appetite and psychiatric effects accompany a boxed warning for abuse, misuse and addiction.
compounds.interactions: MAO inhibitor exposure is contraindicated; other interactions require the specific current product label.

adverse.context: Commonly reported labeled adverse reactions.
Clinically relevant labeled effects; serious cardiac disease changes risk assessment.
Boxed warning; therapeutic indication does not remove this risk.

compounds.name: Atomoxetine
compounds.description: A nonstimulant prescription medicine for ADHD.
compounds.mechanism: Norepinephrine transporter inhibition changes catecholamine signaling.
compounds.findings: Labeled clinical benefit concerns ADHD rather than universal enhancement.
compounds.limits: Clinical response and adverse effects vary by population and metabolic genotype.
compounds.kinetics: CYP2D6 metabolism strongly affects exposure; inhibitors and poor-metabolizer status can increase concentrations.
compounds.risks: GI, appetite, sexual, urinary and cardiovascular effects are important; rare severe liver injury is labeled.
compounds.interactions: MAO inhibitors are contraindicated; strong CYP2D6 inhibitors can substantially raise exposure.

adverse.context: Common labeled reactions; urinary and sexual effects also occur in adults.

adverse.effect: Suicidal ideation in children and adolescents
adverse.context: Boxed warning based on short-term pediatric trial findings.
Rare postmarketing concern in labeling; incidence cannot be estimated precisely.

compounds.name: Selegiline
compounds.description: A monoamine oxidase inhibitor with formulation-specific clinical uses.
compounds.mechanism: Selectivity and systemic monoamine effects depend on formulation and exposure.
compounds.findings: The cited capsule label concerns adjunctive Parkinson treatment; transdermal depression data cannot be transferred unchanged.
compounds.limits: Clinical use for a diagnosed disorder does not establish nootropic benefit.
compounds.kinetics: Oral metabolism and irreversible enzyme inhibition mean blood half-life alone cannot define duration of interactions.
compounds.risks: Nausea, sleep disturbance, hallucinations and postural hypotension have been reported.
compounds.interactions: Serious interactions occur with meperidine and other serotonergic or sympathomimetic medicines; formulation-specific restrictions matter.

adverse.effect: Orthostatic hypotension and loss of balance
adverse.context: Reported in treated Parkinson patients, often with concomitant dopaminergic therapy.
Reported neurological and psychiatric adverse effects.
Hyperthermia, agitation, rigidity and deaths are described with meperidine coadministration.
